body.statement: For every positive finite variance vector \(s\) and every unique-best \(\mu\), one has \(1/C<\rho^\star<1\), and the design \(\mathsf D_{\rho^\star,w}\) satisfies \[\Gamma_{\rho^\star,w}(\mu)\ge G I_w(\mu)>I_w(\mu),\qquad G=\frac{C(1+\eta)}{C+\eta}>1.\] Thus proportional late elimination strictly improves the instancewise error exponent of Kato's variance-aware static equal-gap maximin allocation throughout \((0,\infty)^K\).
body.justification: This is the theorem-level kernel: heterogeneity never creates a positive-variance exception to late-elimination admissibility.
body.gap: Imbens, Qin, and Wager prove common-variance dominance over uniform allocation, while Kato proves equal-gap maximin optimality of a static heteroskedastic allocation; neither proves this strict cross-result dominance.
body.consumer: A multi-arm fundraising experiment with known outcome variances can replace its generalized-Neyman static schedule by the stated two-batch schedule without sacrificing any fixed unique-best instance asymptotically.
